source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is the nonsingular square system Ax=b with A in R^(n x n) and nonzero b in R^n; x denotes its exact solution.

The paper invokes the standard floating-point model, uses fl for computed expressions and hats for computed quantities, defines gamma_k=k*u/(1-k*u), lets superscripts on gamma select the corresponding unit roundoff, and uses generic low-degree polynomials c(n,k). The symbols lesssim and approximately equal mean that negligible second-order terms have been dropped, while much-greater-than and much-less-than are qualitative scale separations.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2, condition number and forward/backward error definitions
source_evidence.observation: The Frobenius condition number is kappa_F(A)=||A^(-1)||_F ||A||_F. Forward error is ||x_hat-x||_2/||x||_2. Normwise backward error is ||b-A*x_hat||_2/(||A||_F||x_hat||_2+||b||_2), equivalently the minimum common relative bound on a Frobenius-norm perturbation of A and a 2-norm perturbation of b.

MOD-GMRES uses A in R^(n x n), b in R^n, a basis Z_k in R^(n x k), and a left preconditioner M_L. It forms A_tilde Z_k, forms M_L^(-1)b, solves a least-squares problem over k coefficients, and forms the approximation Z_k y_k.

The inherited correction-solver contract models the computed product, right-hand side, and least-squares solve by normwise or columnwise perturbations bounded by epsilon_c, epsilon_b, and epsilon_ls, respectively. Condition (3.3) quantifies its columnwise bound for every j<=k+1.

The computed basis action satisfies x_hat_k=fl(Z_k y_hat_k)=Z_k y_hat_k+Delta_x with ||Delta_x||_2<=epsilon_x||Z_k||_F||y_hat_k||_2. The basis must satisfy sigma_min(Z_k) much greater than epsilon_x||Z_k||_F, and all four accuracy parameters must be nonnegative and substantially less than one so second-order terms may be dropped.

The key dimension is the first k<=n for which, for every phi>0 and when k<=n-1, [b_tilde*phi,A_tilde Z_k] is nearly rank deficient at scale c(n,k)(epsilon_c+epsilon_b+epsilon_ls), while A_tilde Z_k remains numerically full rank at that scale. For k=n only the latter condition is required.

Restarted MOD-GMRES is an outer iterative-refinement process indexed by i>=0: compute r_i=b-Ax_i, solve the correction system A d_i=r_i by MOD-GMRES with a possibly iteration-dependent basis size k_i, and update x_(i+1)=x_i+d_i. Its computed residual must satisfy the normwise model (4.1).

Theorem 4.1 additionally assumes the update model (4.2), small residual/update accuracy parameters (4.3), all correction conditions (3.1)-(3.8), and ||x_hat_i||_2 lesssim ||x_hat_(i+1)||_2 lesssim ||x||_2. It gives a forward contraction factor Lambda_1^(i) and the attainable forward level lesssim c(n,k)epsilon_r kappa_F(A)+epsilon_u.

The backward-error part of Theorem 4.1 separately requires sigma_min(A_tilde^(i) Z_(k_i)^(i)) much greater than epsilon_x^(i)||A_tilde^(i)||_F||Z_(k_i)^(i)||_F. It gives contraction factor Lambda_2^(i) and attainable backward level lesssim c(n,k)epsilon_r+epsilon_u.

For MGS-GMRES in unit roundoff u substantially less than one, sigma_min(A) much greater than u||A||_F guarantees a key k<=n. Its proof identifies low-precision product and basis-action parameters and a columnwise backward-stable MGS-Arnoldi least-squares solve with epsilon_ls equivalent to a gamma quantity of index n(k+1).

At the MGS key iteration, the current basis satisfies kappa_2(V_hat_k)<=4/3, sigma_min(V_hat_k)^(-1)<=4/3, and sigma_max(V_hat_k)<=4/3. If orthogonality is lost, k is the first index for which kappa_2(V_hat_(k+1))>4/3 while the current V_hat_k still satisfies those bounds.

source_evidence.anchor: equations (5.17)-(5.18) and conclusion of Theorem 5.2 proof
source_evidence.observation: The MGS proof derives the near-rank-deficiency condition and sigma_min(A V_hat_k)>=3 sigma_min(A)/4 at the key index, thereby discharging conditions (3.5)-(3.8). If orthogonality is never fully lost, k=n supplies the key dimension.

The mixed-precision specialization uses M_L^(i)=I and Z_(k_i)^(i)=V_hat_(k_i)^(i), with the MGS-Arnoldi basis fully formed and stored. Residuals and outer updates are computed in precision u_high; lines 4-7 are the MGS-GMRES correction computation in precision u_low. Theorem 6.3 assumes Lambda=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) much less than one and states both error floors in (6.18). The proof gives the componentwise residual and update models (6.19)-(6.20).

source_evidence.anchor: low-precision residual cast, equation (6.21), and final contraction specialization
source_evidence.observation: For every i>=0 the high-precision residual is cast as r_hat_i'=fl_low(r_hat_i)=r_hat_i+Delta_b^(i), with ||Delta_b^(i)||_2<=u_low||r_hat_i|| as printed, giving epsilon_b^(i)=u_low. The proof invokes Theorem 5.2 to obtain a key k_i, derives xi_1^(i) lesssim c(n,k)u_low in (6.21), and concludes max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i))<=Lambda.

binders: The standing system has dimension n, A in R^(n x n) nonsingular, and 0!=b in R^n. [PDF p. 1, equation (1.1)]

x is the exact solution of Ax=b; x_hat_i, r_hat_i, and d_hat_i denote computed outer iterates, residuals, and corrections. [PDF p. 1, equation (1.1); PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 40, equations (6.19)-(6.20)]
u_high and u_low are the unit roundoffs used, respectively, for the residual/outer update and for all inner correction operations. [PDF p. 40, Theorem 6.3 and Section 6.3 opening specialization]
The outer restart or correction index is universally quantified as i>=0. [PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2 and condition (4.1); PDF p. 41, low-cast paragraph]
For each outer i there is an inner MGS key index k_i<=n; the theorem nevertheless writes the generic polynomial as c(n,k). [PDF p. 27, Theorem 5.2; PDF p. 41, invocation of Theorem 5.2]
Lambda is defined by Lambda=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A). [PDF p. 40, equation (6.17)]
hypotheses: Explicit in Theorem 6.3: mixed precision GMRES computes the residual and outer update with unit roundoff u_high and the rest of its operations with unit roundoff u_low. [PDF p. 40, Theorem 6.3]
Explicit in Theorem 6.3: Lambda=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) is substantially less than one. [PDF p. 40, equation (6.17)]

Algorithm context immediately preceding the theorem allows no prescribed bound on the number of Arnoldi iterations at each restart, so each correction can run until its key k_i is reached. [PDF p. 40, paragraph immediately before Theorem 6.3]

Inherited through Theorem 4.1: for every outer i, the residual and update models (4.1)-(4.3) hold with nonnegative epsilon_r and epsilon_u substantially below one. In the specialization epsilon_r=gamma_n^high and epsilon_u=u_high. [PDF p. 17, equations (4.2)-(4.3) and Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 40, equations (6.19)-(6.20)]

Inherited through Theorem 4.1: for every i, the low-precision correction computation satisfies conditions (3.1)-(3.4), namely bounded product error, bounded low-cast right-hand-side error, a columnwise backward-stable least-squares solve for every j<=k_i+1, and bounded error in forming d_hat_i=Z_(k_i)^(i)y_hat_i. [PDF p. 6, equations (3.1)-(3.3); PDF p. 7, equation (3.4); PDF p. 17, Theorem 4.1]

Inherited through Theorem 4.1: each correction basis is numerically full rank at epsilon_x^(i), all correction accuracy parameters are substantially below one, and a key dimension satisfies (3.7)-(3.8), including the universal quantifier over every scalar phi>0 when k_i<=n-1. [PDF p. 7, equations (3.5)-(3.6); PDF p. 8, equations (3.7)-(3.8); PDF p. 17, Theorem 4.1]
Inherited but not restated in Theorem 6.3: ||x_hat_i||_2 lesssim ||x_hat_(i+1)||_2 lesssim ||x||_2 for every outer i. [PDF p. 17, Theorem 4.1 immediately before equation (4.4)]

Inherited for the backward-error contraction: sigma_min(A Z_(k_i)^(i)) is substantially greater than epsilon_x^(i)||A||_F||Z_(k_i)^(i)||_F. [PDF p. 18, additional hypothesis before equation (4.8); PDF pp. 28-29, equations (5.15) and (5.18)]

Proof-derived inner-solver certificate: sigma_min(A) is substantially greater than u_low||A||_F; the proof states that (6.17) guarantees this, and Theorem 5.2 then supplies a key k_i for every i>=0. [PDF p. 27, equation (5.11); PDF p. 41, paragraph before equation (6.21)]
conclusions: Literal theorem wording: at each iteration the backward and forward errors reduce by a factor stated as at least Lambda until their attainable levels are reached. In context this iteration is the outer restart/correction update i. [PDF p. 40, Theorem 6.3 after equation (6.17); PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2]
The attainable normwise backward error is ||b-A*x_hat||_2/(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_hat||_2) lesssim c(n,k)u_high. [PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
The attainable relative forward error is ||x_hat-x||_2/||x||_2 lesssim c(n,k)u_high kappa_F(A). [PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]

The proof's precise comparison of contraction coefficients is max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i))<=Lambda for every outer iteration for which the inherited hypotheses hold. [PDF p. 41, final displayed inequality]

The result supplies attainable levels and per-outer-step contraction factors but no bound on the number of outer restarts required to reach those levels. [PDF p. 40, sentence preceding Theorem 6.3 and Theorem 6.3]
definitions_and_conventions: A hat marks a computed quantity and fl denotes a computed floating-point expression. [PDF p. 4, first paragraph of Section 2]
gamma_k=k*u/(1-k*u); a superscript on gamma selects the correspondingly subscripted unit roundoff, so gamma_n^high=n*u_high/(1-n*u_high). [PDF p. 4, gamma definition; PDF p. 40, equation (6.19)]
c(n,k) denotes an unspecified polynomial in n and k of low degree that absorbs dimension-dependent constants. [PDF p. 4, paragraph defining c(n,k); PDF p. 40, sentence after equation (6.18)]

lesssim and approximately equal indicate bounds after dropping negligible second-order terms; much-greater-than indicates qualitative scale separation, with low-degree polynomial factors regarded as absorbable. [PDF p. 4, notation paragraph]
kappa_F(A)=||A^(-1)||_F||A||_F for the nonsingular square matrix A. [PDF p. 4, condition-number paragraph]
The key dimension is the first k<=n satisfying (3.7)-(3.8); if k=n, only (3.8) is required. [PDF p. 8, equations (3.7)-(3.8) and following paragraph]
implicit_context: Theorem 6.3 is a specialization of restarted Algorithm 2, not a claim about a single unrestarted MGS-GMRES run. [PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 40, Section 6.3 specialization]
There is no left preconditioner: M_L^(i)=I, and the correction basis is the fully formed and stored MGS-Arnoldi basis Z_(k_i)^(i)=V_hat_(k_i)^(i). [PDF p. 40, first paragraph of printed page 1978]

For each outer i, the inner low-precision problem is A d_i=r_hat_i, with r_hat_i first computed in high precision and then cast to low precision for the MGS-GMRES solve. [PDF p. 40, paragraph after equation (6.20); PDF p. 41, low-cast display]

The invoked MGS proof either chooses k_i=n if orthogonality is never fully lost or chooses the first k_i for which kappa_2(V_hat_(k_i+1))>4/3 while V_hat_(k_i) remains bounded as in (5.15). [PDF p. 28, equations (5.15)-(5.16); PDF p. 29, conclusion of the key-dimension argument]

Algorithm 2 merely says to initialize x_0; Theorem 6.3 gives no separate restriction on x_0, while the invoked Theorem 4.1 imposes the iterate-size comparison. [PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2 line 1; PDF p. 17, Theorem 4.1]

Equations (6.19)-(6.21), the low cast, and the bound on max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i)) are proof-derived details, not clauses printed in the statement of Theorem 6.3. [PDF pp. 40-41, proof of Theorem 6.3]
statement.algorithm_linkage: At outer iteration i, restarted Algorithm 2 computes r_hat_i=fl_high(b-A*x_hat_i), casts this residual to low precision, runs an unpreconditioned fully stored MGS-GMRES correction solve for A d_i=r_hat_i until an inner key k_i is available, forms d_hat_i in low precision, and computes x_hat_(i+1)=fl_high(x_hat_i+d_hat_i). Thus each claimed contraction is tied to one completed outer correction/update, not to an individual Arnoldi step. [PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 40, Section 6.3 specialization and equations (6.19)-(6.20); PDF p. 41, low-cast display]
numerical_model: The overall analysis uses the paper's standard floating-point model and traditional worst-case bounds. [PDF p. 4, opening paragraphs of Section 2]
High-precision residual model: r_hat_i=b-A*x_hat_i+Delta_r_i with componentwise |Delta_r_i|<=gamma_n^high(|b|+|A||x_hat_i|). [PDF p. 40, equation (6.19)]
High-precision update model: x_hat_(i+1)=x_hat_i+d_hat_i+Delta_x_i with componentwise |Delta_x_i|<=u_high|x_hat_(i+1)|. [PDF p. 40, equation (6.20)]
The proof identifies epsilon_r=gamma_n^high and epsilon_u=u_high for Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 40, sentence after equation (6.20)]

Low-precision residual cast: r_hat_i'=fl_low(r_hat_i)=r_hat_i+Delta_b^(i), with ||Delta_b^(i)||_2<=u_low||r_hat_i|| as printed, and epsilon_b^(i)=u_low. [PDF p. 41, low-cast display and following sentence]

The remaining low-precision parameters are those from the MGS-GMRES proof: epsilon_c^(i) is the product-error parameter, epsilon_ls^(i) is of gamma order with index n(k_i+1), and epsilon_x^(i) is of gamma_n order, all using u_low. [PDF p. 27, opening of Theorem 5.2 proof and equation (5.13); PDF p. 41, sentence before equation (6.21)]

At the key dimension, equation (6.21) gives xi_1^(i) lesssim c(n,k)u_low, and the no-preconditioner specialization yields max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i))<=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A). [PDF p. 41, equation (6.21) and final displayed inequality]
error_notions: Forward error compares the computed iterate with the exact solution: ||x_hat-x||_2/||x||_2. [PDF p. 4, forward-error definition; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]

Backward error is the actual normwise backward error of the computed iterate, not merely a residual norm: it is the minimum epsilon for which (A+Delta_A)x_hat=b+Delta_b with ||Delta_A||_F<=epsilon||A||_F and ||Delta_b||_2<=epsilon||b||_2. [PDF p. 4, backward-error definition]
The equivalent backward-error quotient used in Theorem 6.3 is ||b-A*x_hat||_2/(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_hat||_2). [PDF p. 4, backward-error identity; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
Both errors in (6.18) are evaluated using exact A, b, and x and a computed x_hat. [PDF p. 1, equation (1.1); PDF p. 4, error definitions; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
norms: All vector errors and residuals in the theorem's error measures use the Euclidean 2-norm. [PDF p. 4, norm and error definitions; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
Matrix magnitude in the backward-error denominator and perturbation definition uses the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 4, backward-error definition; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
The condition number in (6.17) and the forward floor is the Frobenius condition number kappa_F(A). [PDF p. 4, condition-number definition; PDF p. 40, equations (6.17)-(6.18)]
Equations (6.19)-(6.20) use componentwise absolute values before their conversion to the normwise hypotheses of Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 40, equations (6.19)-(6.20)]
constants_and_indexing: Outer iterations are indexed i>=0, and an update advances i to i+1. [PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 40, equation (6.20)]
For every outer i, the MGS argument existentially supplies an inner key k_i<=n. [PDF p. 27, Theorem 5.2; PDF p. 41, invocation of Theorem 5.2]

The loss-of-orthogonality key uses the offset k_i+1: it is the first index with kappa_2(V_hat_(k_i+1))>4/3 while kappa_2(V_hat_(k_i))<=4/3; if no such loss occurs, k_i=n. [PDF p. 28, equation (5.15) and following paragraph; PDF p. 29, key-dimension conclusion]
The least-squares perturbation condition is columnwise for every j<=k_i+1. [PDF p. 6, equation (3.3)]

The high-precision residual constant is gamma_n^high=n*u_high/(1-n*u_high), while low-precision gamma terms and dimension factors are absorbed into c(n,k). [PDF p. 4, gamma and c(n,k) definitions; PDF p. 40, equation (6.19); PDF p. 41, equation (6.21)]
The theorem does not state a restart count or a fixed inner restart length. [PDF p. 40, paragraph immediately before Theorem 6.3 and Theorem 6.3]
higher_order_terms: The bounds in (6.18) and (6.21) use lesssim, which the paper explicitly defines as dropping negligible second-order terms. [PDF p. 4, notation paragraph; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18); PDF p. 41, equation (6.21)]
The paper does not display an explicit remainder term or big-O expression for the discarded terms in Theorem 6.3. [PDF pp. 40-41, Theorem 6.3 and proof]

The high-precision floors from Theorem 4.1, c(n,k)epsilon_r kappa_F(A)+epsilon_u and c(n,k)epsilon_r+epsilon_u, are specialized using epsilon_r=gamma_n^high and epsilon_u=u_high and absorbed into the c(n,k)u_high levels in (6.18). [PDF p. 17, equation (4.7); PDF p. 18, equation (4.11); PDF p. 40, equations (6.18)-(6.20)]
The condition Lambda much less than one is qualitative rather than a stated numerical threshold. [PDF p. 4, much-greater-than convention; PDF p. 40, equation (6.17)]
exceptional_values: The standing problem excludes singular A and zero b. [PDF p. 1, equation (1.1)]

The proof also requires numerical nonsingularity at low precision, sigma_min(A) much greater than u_low||A||_F, which it says follows from (6.17). [PDF p. 27, equation (5.11); PDF p. 41, paragraph before equation (6.21)]

No explicit treatment of NaNs, infinities, overflow, underflow, subnormal arithmetic, or division by zero appears in the selected passage; the paper only invokes the standard floating-point model. [PDF p. 4, opening of Section 2; PDF pp. 40-41, Theorem 6.3 and proof]

The formula gamma_n^high=n*u_high/(1-n*u_high) and inherited requirement gamma_n^high much less than one implicitly require a nonvanishing denominator and a sufficiently small high-precision rounding level, but Theorem 6.3 does not state a separate numerical inequality such as n*u_high<1. [PDF p. 4, gamma definition; PDF p. 17, condition (4.3); PDF p. 40, equation (6.19)]

undebatable_constraints: The selected result concerns restarted, unpreconditioned, fully stored MGS-GMRES with high-precision residuals and outer updates and low-precision inner corrections. [PDF p. 40, Section 6.3 specialization]
The explicit contraction condition is exactly Lambda=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) much less than one. [PDF p. 40, equation (6.17)]
The result has two distinct conclusions and neither may be omitted: a normwise backward-error floor and a relative forward-error floor. [PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
The backward floor is proportional to u_high without kappa_F(A); the forward floor is proportional to u_high kappa_F(A). [PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
The backward error uses ||A||_F in its denominator and the forward error uses the exact solution's 2-norm. [PDF p. 4, error definitions; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]
The contraction is per completed outer restart/correction update i, with an inner existential key k_i for each i. [PDF p. 16, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 41, key-iteration paragraph]
The residual model uses gamma_n^high and the update model uses u_high, both componentwise as written in (6.19)-(6.20). [PDF p. 40, equations (6.19)-(6.20)]
The high residual is explicitly cast to low precision before the inner solve, contributing epsilon_b^(i)=u_low. [PDF p. 41, low-cast display]
The MGS key satisfies k_i<=n and uses the k_i+1 loss-of-orthogonality offset and the constant 4/3. [PDF pp. 28-29, equations (5.15)-(5.18)]

Applying the cited restarted theorem carries the iterate-size comparison and a separate backward-specific numerical-rank condition, even though Theorem 6.3 does not print them. [PDF p. 17, Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 18, hypothesis before equation (4.8)]
The proof establishes max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i))<=Lambda; a formal contraction statement must preserve this inequality. [PDF p. 41, final displayed inequality]

The lesssim conclusions are first-order bounds with unspecified discarded second-order terms and unspecified low-degree polynomial constants. [PDF p. 4, notation paragraph; PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)]

ambiguities.issue: The symbol k in c(n,k) is not bound in Theorem 6.3, while the restarted proof supplies a potentially different key k_i for each outer i.
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem writes c(n,k) in (6.17)-(6.18), but the proof says that for every i>=0 there exists a key k_i. [PDF p. 40, equations (6.17)-(6.18); PDF p. 41, key-iteration paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must decide whether c is evaluated at each k_i, at a uniform upper bound such as n, or at a separately fixed inner dimension; the paper does not bind this explicitly.

ambiguities.issue: The natural-language phrase reduced by a factor (at least) Lambda is directionally unclear for Lambda<1.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 6.3 uses that wording, while its proof establishes max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i))<=Lambda. Theorem 4.1 uses similar wording for Lambda_1^(i) despite treating it as a contraction coefficient. [PDF p. 40, sentence after (6.17); PDF p. 41, final displayed inequality; PDF p. 17, text before (4.7)]
ambiguities.impact: The proof supports an upper bound on the contraction coefficient, not a lower bound Lambda_1^(i)>=Lambda. A faithful formalization should record the literal wording and the proof inequality rather than silently reverse one.

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 6.3 does not restate or verify the iterate-size hypothesis required by Theorem 4.1.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.1 assumes ||x_hat_i||_2 lesssim ||x_hat_(i+1)||_2 lesssim ||x||_2. Theorem 6.3's proof lists conditions (4.1)-(4.3) and (3.1)-(3.8) but does not mention this comparison. [PDF p. 17, Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 40, first sentence of Theorem 6.3 proof]
ambiguities.impact: A standalone formal theorem needs this as an additional hypothesis or needs a separate derivation; the selected passage does neither explicitly.

ambiguities.issue: The backward-error part of Theorem 4.1 has an additional numerical-rank hypothesis that Theorem 6.3's proof does not explicitly name.
ambiguities.evidence: The additional condition is printed before (4.8). The MGS facts (5.15), (5.18), and the low-precision nonsingularity condition appear intended to imply it, but the final proof only says that applying Theorem 4.1 ends the proof. [PDF p. 18, hypothesis before (4.8); PDF pp. 28-29, equations (5.15) and (5.18); PDF p. 41, final paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: A formal reconstruction must either include this inherited condition or prove it from the MGS key certificate and (6.17).

ambiguities.issue: The paper does not explicitly state an ordering between u_high and u_low or a standalone smallness condition for gamma_n^high in Theorem 6.3.
ambiguities.evidence: The precisions are called high and low, but the theorem gives only (6.17), which involves u_low. The invoked Theorem 4.1 separately requires epsilon_r=gamma_n^high and epsilon_u=u_high to be substantially below one. [PDF p. 40, Theorem 6.3 and equations (6.17), (6.19)-(6.20); PDF p. 17, condition (4.3)]
ambiguities.impact: One should not silently add u_high<u_low, although practical interpretation suggests it; validity of the inherited high-precision model still requires gamma_n^high to be defined and small.

ambiguities.issue: The right-hand norm in the low-precision cast bound is printed without a norm subscript.
ambiguities.evidence: The display on printed page 1979 reads ||Delta_b^(i)||_2<=u_low||r_hat_i||, whereas condition (3.2), which the text says this satisfies, uses a 2-norm on both sides. [PDF p. 41, low-cast display; PDF p. 6, equation (3.2)]
ambiguities.impact: Interpreting the right-hand side as a 2-norm is strongly suggested but is inherited or inferred rather than typographically explicit in that display.

ambiguities.issue: The prose introducing condition (3.4) gives the coefficient vector y_hat_k the dimension R^n, which conflicts with the matrix product Z_k y_hat_k for Z_k in R^(n x k).
ambiguities.evidence: Printed page 1945 says Z_k in R^(n x k) and y_hat_k in R^n immediately before (3.4), while Algorithm 1 solves a least-squares problem with k coefficients and then forms Z_k y_k. [PDF p. 7, text before equation (3.4); PDF p. 5, Algorithm 1]
ambiguities.impact: Unless k=n, the displayed product requires y_hat_k in R^k. This appears to be a source typo and must not be silently treated as a genuine R^n binder.

ambiguities.issue: The symbols much less than and lesssim are deliberately nonquantitative.
ambiguities.evidence: Section 2 defines the scale notation informally and says lesssim drops negligible second-order terms; neither (6.17) nor (6.18) supplies a numerical threshold or explicit remainder. [PDF p. 4, notation paragraph; PDF p. 40, equations (6.17)-(6.18)]
ambiguities.impact: The paper passage is not by itself an exact epsilon-delta inequality with fixed constants; any exact formal bound requires an explicit interpretation or strengthening.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase unbounded number of Arnoldi iterations does not specify an executable stopping rule or fixed restart length.
ambiguities.evidence: The paragraph before Theorem 6.3 says the analysis allows an unbounded number of Arnoldi iterations at each restart, while the proof relies on eventually reaching a key k_i<=n. [PDF p. 40, paragraph immediately before Theorem 6.3; PDF p. 41, key-iteration paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: The theorem does not automatically cover a practical fixed-length restart that stops before k_i; nor does it provide a computable criterion for recognizing the key dimension.

contract_plain_english: For a nonsingular real square system Ax=b, run the restarted mixed-precision algorithm whose outer residual and iterate update are standard high-precision operations and whose unpreconditioned, fully stored MGS-GMRES correction solve is performed in low precision, including a cast of the high-precision residual to low precision. [PDF p. 1, equation (1.1); PDF p. 40, Section 6.3 specialization; PDF p. 41, low-cast display] If Lambda=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) is much less than one, and the inherited hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 and the MGS key-dimension argument hold at every outer restart, then the proof bounds both outer contraction coefficients by Lambda. [PDF pp. 17-18, Theorem 4.1; PDF pp. 27-29, Theorem 5.2 proof; PDF pp. 40-41, equations (6.17) and (6.21) and final factor inequality] The eventual computed iterate has normwise backward error lesssim c(n,k)u_high and relative 2-norm forward error lesssim c(n,k)u_high kappa_F(A). [PDF p. 40, equation (6.18)] These are first-order attainable levels with unspecified low-degree polynomial constants and discarded second-order terms, not exact equalities or a bound on the number of restarts. [PDF p. 4, notation paragraph; PDF p. 40, Theorem 6.3]
